title: The Hidden Ocean
narration: Imagine an ocean with more than twice the water of every sea on Earth, but it's not on Earth. It's hidden beneath the cracked ice of a distant moon, six hundred seventy-one thousand kilometers from Jupiter. How can it stay liquid?
visual_goal: A dramatic zoom into Europa's cracked ice surface, then a cutaway revealing a dark, vast ocean below.

title: Jupiter's Grip
narration: What keeps that ocean from freezing solid? The answer is a gravitational tug-of-war, a moon that stretches and flexes like a rubber band. Europa is tidally locked, so one side always faces Jupiter. Its orbit is slightly lopsided. Each pass stretches the moon, flexing its interior.
visual_goal: Show Europa orbiting Jupiter with an exaggerated eccentric orbit, flexing and straining.

title: The Heat Engine
narration: That friction generates heat. An eccentricity of point zero zero nine seems tiny, but it's enough to keep an ocean liquid, sixty to one hundred fifty kilometers deep.
visual_goal: Diagram showing tidal flexing generating heat, with an arrow indicating heat rising to the ocean.

title: A Young Surface
narration: This world is not frozen in time. Its surface is marked by long, linear cracks and few craters, a sign of recent geological activity. Scientists estimate the surface is only twenty to one hundred eighty million years old, a blink in the four point six-billion-year history of our solar system.
visual_goal: Slow pan across Europa's surface, highlighting cracks and ridges with minimal craters.

title: The First Evidence
narration: In nineteen ninety-five, Galileo arrived. For eight years, it orbited Jupiter. Its data pointed to a hidden ocean, changing everything.
visual_goal: Historic footage of Galileo spacecraft, then a cut to its magnetometer readings showing a induced field.

title: The Clues
narration: What did Galileo find? Ice, salts, sulfuric acid, each clue adds to a story. Tidal heating, a magnetic field that flickers, they all point to one conclusion: a vast, salty ocean hidden beneath the ice.
visual_goal: Montage of Europa's surface composition, tidal flexing, and magnetic field lines, with subtle puzzle-like assembly.

title: The Deep Ocean
narration: More than twice the water of all Earth's oceans. The depth? sixty to one hundred fifty kilometers. There, in the dark, could life exist?
visual_goal: A cross-section of Europa showing a deep ocean, with faint bioluminescent specks in the dark.

title: The Clock Ticks
narration: In October two thousand twenty-four, Europa Clipper launched, a six-year journey. Arrival at Jupiter: April two thousand thirty.
visual_goal: Launch footage of Europa Clipper, then a fast-forward animation of its trajectory to Jupiter.

title: The Arrival
narration: After arrival, the probe will execute dozens of close flybys, peering through the ice for signs of a habitable ocean.
visual_goal: Europa Clipper flying over Europa's surface, with instruments scanning the ice.

title: The Question
narration: If that ocean has the chemistry, the heat, and the time, four point six billion years, could life have found a foothold? [pause] We are about to find out.
visual_goal: A hopeful image of Europa's surface with a subtle glow from beneath, hinting at life.
